Andorra participated at the [[2000 Summer Olympics]] in [[Sydney]], Australia, held between 15 September and 1 October 2000. The country's participation in Sydney marked its seventh appearance at the [[Summer Olympics]] since its debut in [[Andorra at the 1976 Summer Olympics|1976]].

The Andorran team consisted of athletes [[Antoni Bernadó]] and [[Silvia Felipo]], shooter [[Joan Tomàs (sport shooter)|Joan Tomàs]], and swimmers [[Santiago Deu]] and [[Meritxell Sabaté]]. Bernadó was the country's flag-bearer during the [[2000 Summer Olympics opening ceremony|opening ceremony]]. Andorra did not win a medal in the Games, and as of these Games, the country had not earned a Summer Olympic medal.

== Background ==
The [[Andorran Olympic Committee]] was set up in 1967 and was recognized by the [[International Olympic Committee]] in 1975.<ref name="Andorra">{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/countries/AND|title=Andorra at the Olympics|work=[[Olympedia]]|access-date=1 June 2024}}</ref> The nation made its first [[Summer Olympics]] appearance at the [[1976 Summer Olympics]] held in [[Montreal]], Canada. This edition of the Games marked the nation's seventh appearance at the Summer Games.<ref name="Andorra"/>

The [[2000 Summer Olympics]] were held in [[Sydney]], Australia  held between 15 September and 1 October 2000.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/sydney-2000|title=Sydney 2000|work=[[Olympics.com]]|access-date=3 February 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/editions/25|title=2000 Summer Olympics|work=[[Olympedia]]|access-date=3 February 2024}}</ref> The Andorran delegation consisted of five athletes.<ref name="Result">{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/editions/25|title=Andorra at the 2000 Summer Olympics|work=[[Olympedia]]|access-date=3 February 2024}}</ref><ref name="SR">{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/AND/summer/2000/|title=Andorra at 2000 Summer Olympics|work=Sports Reference|access-date=1 June 2001|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417093548/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/AND/summer/2000/|archive-date=17 April 2020}}</ref> [[Antoni Bernadó]] was the country's flag-bearer in the [[2000 Summer Olympics Parade of Nations|Parade of Nations]] during the [[2000 Summer Olympics opening ceremony|opening ceremony]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/flagbearers?edition_id=25|title=Flag bearers at the 2000 Summer Olympics|work=[[Olympedia]]|access-date=3 February 2024}}</ref> Andorra did not win a medal in the Games, and as of these Games, the country had not earned a Summer Olympic medal.<ref name="Andorra"/><ref name="SR"/>

== Athletics ==
[[File:Toni_Bernadó_-_2012_Olympic_Marathon.jpg|thumb|upright=0.6|[[Antoni Bernadó]] participated in the [[Athletics at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon|men's marathon]] event.]]
{{main|Athletics at the 2000 Summer Olympics}}
Andorra qualified two athletes for the [[Athletics at the 2000 Summer Olympics|athletics]] event at the Games.<ref name="Result"/> In the [[Athletics at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon|men's marathon]], [[Antoni Bernadó]] was ranked 49th amongst the 81 finishers with a time of 2:23.03.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/65407|title=Results, men's marathon|work=[[Olympedia]]|access-date=1 June 2024}}</ref> In the [[Athletics at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Women's 1500 metres|women's 1500 m]] event, Silvia Felipo finished 13th in the heats and failed to advance to the finals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/65752|title=Results, women's 1500m|work=[[Olympedia]]|access-date=1 June 2024}}</ref>

== Shooting ==
{{main|Shooting at the 2000 Summer Olympics}}
Andorra qualified one athlete for the [[Shooting at the 2000 Summer Olympics|sports shooting]] event at the Games.<ref name="Result"/> In the [[Shooting at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Men's trap|men's trap]], [[Joan Tomàs (sport shooter)|Joan Tomàs]] was ranked 39th and second last with a score of 101 in the qualification event.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/51950|title=Results, men's trap|work=[[Olympedia]]|access-date=1 June 2024}}</ref> In the [[Athletics at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Women's 1500 metres|women's 1500 m]] event, Silvia Felipo finished 13th in the heats and failed to advance to the finals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/65752|title=Results, women's 1500m|work=[[Olympedia]]|access-date=1 June 2024}}</ref>

== Swimming ==
{{main|Swimming at the 2000 Summer Olympics}}
Andorra were allocated two quota places for the [[Swimming at the 2000 Summer Olympics|swimming]] event at the Games.<ref name="Result"/> In the [[Swimming at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Men's 200 metre freestyle|men's 200 m freestyle]] [[Santiago Deu]] was classified 51st and failed to advance to the finals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/8368|title=Results, men's 200 m freestyle|work=[[Olympedia]]|access-date=1 June 2024}}</ref> In the [[Swimming at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Women's 200 metre individual medley|women's medley]] event, [[Meritxell Sabaté]] finished 35th in the heats and failed to advance to the finals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/8676|title=Results, women's 200m individual medley|work=[[Olympedia]]|access-date=1 June 2024}}</ref>
